document_title: The Ladder Stops at Fifth Grade
deck_summary_line: The minute ladder as drafted, the AI drafts with no grade line, and the seven documents that moved in one day.
post_copy:
15 minutes a day. That is the routine technology cap a Kenai Peninsula Borough School District draft would set for kindergarten.

The draft reached the Policy Review Committee on August 3rd. For secondary schools it says "routine daily technology limits are not established". Grades 6 through 12 get adjectives instead. It never mentions AI.

This page covered the district's AI rulebook in July. The minute ladder is new since then.

The regulation the district ties to "the inclusion of AI" was on that same agenda in two competing drafts. Neither appears to draw a grade line. Nothing is adopted.

Students start August 19th districtwide.

The minute ladder as drafted, the AI drafts with no grade line, and the seven documents that moved in one day.

Does the AI regulation need grade lines too, or is one standard right for a five year old and a senior?

#AKedu #KenaiPeninsula #AIinSchools

slides.body: Alaska's Strategic Framework, Artificial Intelligence for K-12, sets seven guiding principles. It is the document the district group compared its own material against last fall. No published source makes it binding on the district.
